title: Bradford skin cancer waiting times cut by new AI technology
key_facts: St Luke's Hospital, Bradford, adopted the DERM AI system in April
32 patients seen per session instead of 24
Unnecessary biopsies down about 10%, per the hospital trust
Skin Analytics claims 99.9% accuracy at ruling out melanoma
Every image is double-checked by a clinician
NICE recommended it for NHS use for three years while evidence is collected; used in 40 NHS trusts
About 5,000 suspected skin cancer referrals a year in Bradford, about 8% (400) malignant
quote_evidence: The quick scanning means that 32 patients can be seen in each session, compared to 24 before AI was introduced.
The company behind the technology, Skin Analytics, claims the AI is 99.9% accurate at ruling out melanoma cases.
In Bradford, every image is double-checked by a clinician
why_it_matters_hint: Shows early NHS results from AI skin checks, mostly from the trust and the vendor.
notes: Accuracy figure is the company's claim; results are early and from the trust.
